result:
Post revisions are in place and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not run the app or exercise the routes over HTTP.

Saving the edit form now keeps the post's previous title, excerpt and body as a revision, inside the same D1 batch as the update. The new `post_revisions` table comes from a generated migration (`db/migrations/20261019223913_unknown_rockslide.sql`). `GET /posts/:id/revisions` is a page (`pages/posts/[id]/revisions.server.ts` and `.tsx`) listing revisions newest first, linked from the post page for the author. `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` lives in `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`, since a page action can't express that path. It keeps the current version as a new revision, then restores the chosen one and redirects to the post. Both routes send guests to `/login`, return 403 to non-authors, and return 404 for a revision that belongs to another post. Delete now removes the post's revisions in the same batch as the post. The shared helpers are in `lib/posts.ts`.

One thing I noticed and did not change: `DELETE /posts/:id` never checks authorship, so any signed-in user can delete any post. It's outside this request, but it's worth a separate fix.
